title: Beechcraft Bonanza A36 — Emergency Procedures
description: Emergency procedures for the Beechcraft Bonanza A36 with Continental IO-550 fuel-injected engine, constant-speed propeller, and retractable tricycle gear. Memory items are marked. All airspeeds and numerical limits must come from the specific aircraft POH. The IO-550 is fuel-injected — carburetor ice is not applicable. Retractable gear requires specific gear-unsafe and emergency-extension procedures; locate the emergency gear extension handle before flight. Not a substitute for recurrent emergency training or qualified instruction in type.

source.notes: No manufacturer document consulted. Written from general familiarity with the type.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities, or other numerical limitations — all must come from the specific aircraft POH.
Equipment variations exist across A36 airframes. Verify every item against the specific aircraft and its POH before use.

rights.notes: Manufacturer POH remains under copyright. This file does not reproduce its wording or selection of items.

sections.title: Engine Failure on Takeoff — Before or At Liftoff

items.text: Throttle
Brakes — apply to stop within remaining runway
Mixture
Ignition switch
Master switch
Fuel selector
Do not attempt a turnback to the runway at low altitude. If airborne with insufficient runway remaining, land ahead or within a narrow arc of the runway heading on the best available surface.
Occupants — advise to brace

sections.title: Engine Failure After Takeoff — Airborne, Low Altitude

items.text: Airspeed — establish best glide without delay
Landing area — choose a suitable surface ahead within glide range
Fuel selector
Mixture
Ignition switch
Throttle — advance to full if restart attempted
Landing gear — extend when landing surface is assured and within normal gear extension speed
If restart fails — secure engine; follow forced landing checklist
Airspeed — establish best glide
Landing area — identify best field within glide range
Fuel selector
Mixture
Ignition switch
Throttle — advance to full for restart attempt
Boost pump
If restart attempt fails — confirm mixture to idle cutoff, ignition off, fuel selector off
Squawk and communicate — declare emergency
Proceed to forced landing checklist
Mixture
Fuel selector
Master switch
Throttle
items.response: OPEN FULLY — starve any remaining combustion of fuel-air

items.text: Airspeed — if fire persists, increase airspeed within Vne to attempt extinguishment by slipstream
Declare emergency and communicate position
Proceed to forced landing checklist — land immediately
items.response: FORCED LANDING CHECKLIST; SHORTEST POSSIBLE TIME TO LANDING

items.text: Throttle
items.response: FULL OPEN BRIEFLY — draw fire back into engine if fire is in induction

items.text: Mixture
Fuel selector
Ignition switch
Master switch
Evacuate — all occupants exit and move upwind away from aircraft
Fire extinguisher — use if available and fire is accessible without risk
items.response: EXTINGUISHER USED IF SAFE TO DO SO

items.text: Emergency services
Master switch
Avionics master switch
All individual switches — turn off all electrical equipment
Fresh air — open vents or window to ventilate cockpit if conditions permit
Fire extinguisher — if source is identified and fire is active
If smoke clears — restore master switch; bring up essential circuits one at a time to identify the faulty circuit
items.response: FAULTY CIRCUIT IDENTIFIED AND LEFT OFF

items.text: Land as soon as practicable
Power — reduce to minimum needed for flight
Oil temperature — check for rise confirming actual oil starvation
items.response: MONITOR; RISING TEMP CONFIRMS OIL LOSS

items.text: Land as soon as possible — do not continue if oil temperature rises or pressure remains zero
Declare emergency and advise ATC of situation
Zero oil pressure with rising temperature indicates imminent engine seizure. Anticipate engine failure and prepare for forced landing before the engine stops.
Forced landing preparation — if engine seizes or stops, execute forced landing checklist
Airspeed — best glide maintained throughout
Field selection — choose longest suitable surface aligned with wind; aim long with room to manoeuvre
Squawk and transmit — declare emergency, give position and intentions
items.response: SQUAWK 7700; POSITION TRANSMITTED ON 121.5 OR ATC FREQUENCY

items.text: Fuel selector
Mixture
Ignition switch
Master switch — leave on until short final to maintain flap operation; off before touchdown
items.response: ON THROUGH FLAP EXTENSION; OFF BEFORE TOUCHDOWN

items.text: Landing gear — extend when landing on the chosen field is assured; use emergency extension if normal system fails
items.response: GEAR DOWN AND LOCKED; THREE GREEN CONFIRMED

items.text: Flaps — extend on final as altitude permits
items.response: EXTENDED PER FIELD AND ENERGY MANAGEMENT

items.text: Seat belts and shoulder harnesses — tighten for all occupants
Doors — unlatch just before touchdown to prevent jamming in structure
Occupants — advise to brace for landing
Airspeed — slow to gear operating speed range and confirm within Vlo
items.response: AT OR BELOW Vlo PER POH

items.text: Gear handle — cycle up then down; allow full extension time
Gear position indicators — check all three lights
items.response: NOTE ANY MISSING OR RED LIGHT

items.text: Circuit breakers — check gear-related breakers for popped breakers
items.response: RESET IF POPPED; ONE ATTEMPT ONLY

items.text: Gear warning horn — confirm horn sounds with power reduced and handle down
If normal system fails — proceed to emergency gear extension checklist
Advise ATC of gear uncertainty and request a low pass if available for visual confirmation
items.response: ATC ADVISED; VISUAL CONFIRMATION REQUESTED IF AVAILABLE

items.text: Airspeed — reduce to below Vlo and maintain safe manoeuvreing margin
Gear handle
Emergency gear extension handle — locate on the floor or console per aircraft configuration
Emergency extension — pull or turn handle per POH placarded instructions to release gear free-fall locks
Allow time for gravity and airstream to extend and lock all three gear legs
Gear position indicators
items.response: THREE GREEN CONFIRMED; IF ANY LIGHT MISSING, TREAT AS UNSAFE

items.text: If less than three green lights after emergency extension, the gear may not be down and locked on all legs. Consider a low-speed fly-by for visual confirmation, and plan for a possible partial-gear or gear-up landing.
Land as soon as possible — advise ATC and emergency services of gear status
